schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
remit: THE EXPLICIT REMIT (Akien, verbatim): 'Its job is to save you tokens in exploring the issue in the same way the prebuild step does for coding. And to keep getting better over time.' The inspector is the DEBUGGING ANALOG OF THE PREBUILD STEP: prebuild pre-processes so CC (the expensive resolver) spends tokens only on the novel coding; the inspector pre-processes a red so CC spends tokens only on the novel diagnosis — never on a second exploration to gather data the first pass should have carried (Law 1, the cocoon). 'Gets better over time' is monotonic and physical: every gap it learns is one fewer second-exploration forever, so the tokens it saves only rise. Those two sentences ARE the falsifier — everything below serves them or it is dead weight.
what: THE SMART READER of DiagnosticBase's dumb breadcrumbs, factored (Akien) into the three parts of the diagnostic surface. (1) LOGGING — gates emit microsecond-stamped breadcrumbs (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py); that is STATE, so its durable home is instance-space (~/.cairn/, cache-class json log). That home EXISTS as of 2026-08-12 (ticket a-record-reaches-disk): BreadcrumbLog in log.py, appending one JSON line per record to <instance space>/diagnostics.jsonl — one trail per owning device instance, addressed through cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path, never hand-spelled. Mailbox stays exactly what it always said it was — the in-memory STAND-IN, a proof fixture so an emitter->receiver->inspector chain runs end to end — and the strongest evidence that it was honest about what it stood for is that the disk log answers the SAME TWO CONTRACTS (receive_diagnostic / records) and drops into Inspector.inspect with inspector.py untouched, its imports still exactly copy/json/pathlib. The two coexist; neither replaces the other. (2) PROBE — when a watched thing happens (a red, a watched gate-contact) a probe FIRES 'inspect now'; event, not poll (the shrinking-footprint discipline). (3) INSPECTOR — this module. It REACTS to the probe: applies FILTERS to the log and produces FINDINGS. FILTERS are predicates (predicate(record)->bool) conjoined at inspection time inside a fired run (never a standing scan/firehose): by_pointer (the primary — one item's whole transaction, the complete-first-pass slice) and by_gate are built because they have consumers; by_time_band / by_severity are filed edges the abstraction admits without a query-language built ahead of one. FINDINGS are json whose entire audience is CC: the ordered, isolated transaction slice (every emitted value carried, source deep-copied never mutated) PLUS the COMPLETENESS finding.
why: Instantiates the concept-piece I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass — findings that resolve the issue on the FIRST pass, a method Akien has proven over decades (2007 test framework, UU, Trouble Tickets; his first-reach debugging tool; half-day->10min). DiagnosticBase.emit left the intelligence OUT of the breadcrumb deliberately (Law 1 — the diagnostic surface's inference compiled ONCE, here, the inference_domain move); this is that one place. The learning-loop the inspector CARRIES makes the findings self-teaching (I-learns-its-gates pointed at the diagnostic surface): completeness rises monotonically and no learned gap recurs — which is exactly 'gets better over time' made physics.
invoke: In code: from cairn.machines.diagnostic_inspector import Inspector, by_pointer, by_gate, CompletenessRegistry, Mailbox. Wire a receiver as a DiagnosticBase receiver (dev.set_diagnostic_receiver(box)) — a Mailbox to hold records in memory for the length of one attached session, or `from cairn.machines.diagnostic_inspector.log import BreadcrumbLog; dev.set_diagnostic_receiver(BreadcrumbLog('<device>', 0))` for the durable trail at <instance space>/diagnostics.jsonl (roots= is injectable so a proof never touches the live tree); on a fired probe, findings = Inspector(registry).inspect(box.records(), by_pointer(ptr)[, by_gate(g)]) — filters conjoin. Fold a miss: inspector.record_miss(gate, key) ('learned' first time, 'recurred' after). Persist learned completeness: inspector.registry.save(path) / CompletenessRegistry.load(path). Prove: python3 cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py and python3 cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/proofs/test_breadcrumb_log.py (exit 0 = green).
for_whom: CC, DURING DEBUGGING — and this one is SETTLED, exempted by name when Akien had every other findings-emitter's consumer sorted (Akien, 2026-08-06): 'we have to sort the consumer for every single one of them except the diagnostic inspector. because that's the one you'll use when we need to do debugging. and it's backed by 2 decades of akien's experience as the first tool i reach for.' Recorded here so the exemption is a fact on disk rather than something a reader has to have been present for. Two things follow. (1) THE STANDING IS PROVENANCE, NOT PREFERENCE: the shape of these findings — the whole ordered transaction slice, isolated, complete on first pass — is what twenty years of reaching for this tool first taught him it must be. That is measured experience arriving as design, so a proposal to reshape the findings is arguing with the evidence, not with a habit. (2) THE CONSUMER BEING A MIND, NOT A MACHINE, IS THE POINT: these findings exist to keep CC from a second exploration, so their falsifier is token cost, and the CompletenessRegistry learning what a gate must carry is that falsifier's own feedback loop. Contrast build_inspector, whose findings are consumed by a machine (the emit chokepoint) and therefore must be refusable rather than readable — the two shapes differ BECAUSE the consumers differ, which is Akien's distinguisher: 'these two are emitted for different consumers is the difference.' WHAT IT OWES THAT CONSUMER, specified by Akien 2026-08-06 when he corrected the reading that this was merely 'a component whose consumer happens to be CC': 'the diagnostic inspector's output is actually something you will consume. just as the pre-build step is the orientation about what to build... this is a key piece of what you need to debug. so when you get an inspection report, it should tell you things like where it failed, and what the failure was... what variables were in play and important. what things is it operating on there. so that you have a complete picture of exactly what happened millisecond to millisecond leading up to the failure, and everything that was involved. you're the consumer and that's what it should tell you. and if it doesn't tell you that, then you need to tell it what it does need to tell you.' THE LAST SENTENCE IS THE LOOP, AND IT NAMES CC AS THE ONE WHO CLOSES IT: record_miss() is not a documented feature, it is the thing the consumer is expected to USE when a report reads thin. A report that left me re-exploring, and no record_miss folded from it, is the falsifier — not the thin report itself, which is only the first miss (learning signal, per the intention).
node_class: code-seam — berths in cairn/ (class-space) beside the breadcrumbs DiagnosticBase.emit sends. Born as children a (the crawler) + b (the learning-loop) of the ticket, then REFACTORED from diagnostic_interpreter/assemble(records, pointer) to the inspector/filters/findings shape Akien named — the same proven engine, re-seated on the true intention (an inspector reacting to a probe, filters composing, findings for CC). Child c (the `cairn diagnose <pointer>` CLI face, via cairn-command) is the LEAST-USED secondary access path (Akien: 'of all the secondary access paths, almost certainly the one I'm least likely to use') — buildable, lowest priority; the engine is the substance.
how_it_learns: YES — learning is its WHOLE SECOND HALF and the 'gets better over time' half of the remit, not an add-on. The CompletenessRegistry the Inspector CARRIES across inspections IS a learns-its-gates instance whose endpoint is the diagnostic findings: its GATE is a transition-class, its EVIDENCE is a resolver hitting a gap the findings should have carried, and its CONFIDENCE-MOVE is folding that key into what the class's findings must include (record_miss). The special-class falsifier is the learning rule made physics: a FIRST miss is a feed-forward signal ('learned'); an already-learned key absent from a later findings is a RECURRENCE, surfaced LOUD (inspect's completeness.recurrences, complete=False) — the terminal falsifier, a Law 1 defect it refuses to let pass silently (the surface failed to save the tokens it had already learned to save). Distinct endpoint from the decision-autonomy store in CairnCommons/learning/ (which learns whether CC may ACT); kin, cross-referenced, NOT merged — a distinct store with a distinct key. Its horizon: where learned completeness durably lives (a commons git-JSON store vs CC's shim when shims land) — injected path today, real home a filed edge. AND THE FIRST MISS WAS CAUGHT BY THE HUMAN HALF, 2026-08-06 — worth recording because it is the loop firing outside the code. SEED claimed to carry the list from I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass and had dropped two items in translation: `source`, and 'every value at every transition and boundary that bears on the fault'. Akien re-stated both from his side without having read the file ('what variables were in play and important. what things is it operating on there'). `source` rejoined SEED; the every-value clause became a CHECK rather than a key, because requiring the literal key 'values' would be missing by construction (_completeness scans INTO values and excludes the wrapper) — red forever, teaching nothing. A tooth now reds if SEED drifts from the intention's sentence again. AND A SECOND MISS, SAME DAY, ON THE READING RATHER THAN THE DATA (see edge (f)): CC treated an on-demand instrument's absence of callers as an unbuilt supply chain. The generalisable check, since the measurement itself was fine and only the interpretation was wrong: before reporting that nothing calls a component, ask whether it is supposed to be called by STANDING CODE or PLACED BY A HAND. For the second kind, zero call sites is the resting state and counting it as a gap manufactures work.
traces_to: THE REMIT (save CC tokens exploring an issue as prebuild does for coding; get better over time) — the charter's own first field, Akien-stated
I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass (the concept-piece this instantiates — the findings deliver all resolve-data on the first pass)
Law 1 (a second exploration to gather more failure data is re-deriving the settled — the waste the complete findings kills; and the inspector's inference is compiled ONCE here, the cocoon)

Law 7 SHARPENED (the diagnostic surface is not merely loud but COMPLETE on first emission; a learned recurrence is surfaced LOUD, never silent; the findings are a transient surface, the RESOLUTION CC produces is the record of truth)
I-learns-its-gates (the learning-loop is gate-learning pointed at the diagnostic surface — a distinct endpoint: what the findings must CARRY)
Law 6 (the emission stays a thin pointer; the inspector reads and never emits, never copies the ticket, never mutates its source records — the dumb-breadcrumb / smart-reader split)
cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py (DiagnosticBase.emit — the breadcrumb this crawls; its docstring named this inspector as 'the next build')
owner: CC owns the diagnostic_inspector code + its proof and gates writes to them. The inspector READS breadcrumbs and logs; it never emits and never owns the tickets it points at (Law 6 — owned data stays with its owner; only the pointer crosses, and the inspector follows it, it does not copy).
proof: proofs/test_inspector.py — eight teeth a hollow inspector could not pass: findings filter ONE pointer's transaction ordered by the 6th-decimal stamp and isolated (real DiagnosticBase emissions, other pointers excluded — Law 6); FILTERS COMPOSE (by_pointer AND by_gate narrows to the conjunction — 'filters' is plural, not a single hardcoded match); it reads without mutating (deep-copied slice); a first miss is 'learned' and folded forward so the next findings require it, routed THROUGH the Inspector (the inspector is what gets better — Law 1); a learned gap that recurs is complete=False and named in recurrences (LOUD, Law 7); a complete findings is clean; record_miss distinguishes 'learned' from 'recurred'; learned completeness save->load round-trips (a missing file is an empty registry, not an error). Green bare (python3) and sealed under the tester; VALIDATION persisted beside-code at validations/test_inspector.json.  AND proofs/test_breadcrumb_log.py — ten teeth, 39 assertions, sealed under the tester in netns (validations/test_breadcrumb_log.json). THE TOOTH THE TROUBLE DEMANDED is a_record_emitted_in_one_process_is_read_back_in_another: the emit happens in a CHILD process which then exits, and the parent reads the record back off the file with the timestamp matching byte-for-byte — a same-process assertion would have passed on the in-memory hold and proved nothing. Beside it: the write appends and never rewrites (the first record's bytes survive the second, and no .tmp is produced); two devices get two trails (Law 6 on the FILE); the address comes from the one owner (AST-checked — no Path.home(), no literal '.cairn' outside the docstring, which is where the first draft of this tooth matched its own prose and went red for the wrong reason); running the proof writes nothing into the live tree, so the acceptance read-back cannot be something the proof seeded; the disk log drops into Inspector.inspect unchanged; and the two failure modes stay DIFFERENT — an unserializable payload degrades with the crossing still recorded, a corrupt trail is loud by line number. The roster is DERIVED from the module's own globals, not hand-listed, so a tooth added and never wired to the runner cannot hide.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) the findings are INCOMPLETE by construction — they drop an emitted value or bleed in another pointer's records (not a faithful, isolated slice); (2) filters do NOT compose — a second filter is ignored so the conjunction is a lie; (3) the learning-loop records a miss but never changes the next findings (learning theater — the fold is a no-op); (4) an already-learned gap recurs and the findings stay SILENT about it (the terminal falsifier — must be loud, Law 7); (5) the inspector grows an emit path (it becomes a second emitter, collapsing the dumb-breadcrumb / smart-reader split — Law 6); (6) it mutates its source records (it must read, never write, what it is handed); (7) the learned-completeness store is merged into the decision-autonomy gate-store (two distinct learnings collapsed); (8) the inspector runs as a STANDING SCAN rather than reacting to a fired probe (the firehose/poll the shrinking-footprint discipline rejects).
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)

WHAT THIS DOES NOT UNBLOCK, and the distinction is the whole of edge (f): a durable source now exists, so child c (`cairn diagnose`) is no longer BLOCKED — but it is still unbuilt and unasked-for, and 'no longer blocked' is not 'now owed'. WHAT MOVED IN THE ADDRESS: this edge said ~/.cairn/ and meant the top level, which was the reading before Akien ruled ownership over depth on 2026-08-12 — a device's own trail is that device's state, so it lands under devices/<name>/<instance>/ and the machine-scoped ~/.cairn/logs/ keeps only what answers 'what is true of this machine'. The 30-day fat tier this edge also named is NOT built: nothing rotates, nothing expires, and an expiry policy written before a single record existed would be the reverse of build-minimal. That half stands open, here, deliberately.

(c) the durable home for learned completeness (a commons git-JSON store vs CC's shim when shims land) is a filed edge — the store path is injected, proven against a temp

(g) THE INDEPENDENCE IS ONE REASONED DISTINCTION, NOT A LAW — ruling 2026-08-06-the-diagnostic-fork-is-one-allowed-distinction, which retired 2026-08-05-an-inspector-may-not-depend-on-what-it-inspects. WHAT STANDS, in Akien's words: 'the diagnostic inspector MUST be a distinct piece of code, but built on the same principles... logging for the logging system itself has to work even if logging itself is broken.' This device and build_inspector are ONE MECHANISM WITH DIFFERENT DATA — same model, same finding shape, same vocabulary — and the code is forked anyway, for that one reason and no other. WHAT DOES NOT STAND, and this charter asserted it for a day: 'an inspector may not be built on what it inspects.' Akien ruled that conceptually false on 2026-08-06 — 'it's not physics. it's how things happen to be at the moment' — and gave the counterexample: 'i am the first line inspector for my monkey (physical self). my various doctors are my second line inspectors. but i have also trained myself to do that.' Self-inspection is a TRAINED skill with a second line behind it, and Cairn has built neither; the fork is what we do until we have. He said 'so far, this is true', and 'so far' is load-bearing — this edge is expected to expire, not to harden. THE DANGER REMAINS TIDINESS: the duplication looks exactly like a Law 1 defect, and CC tried to merge it on 2026-08-05 from reading the two docstrings. Prose will not hold it (Law 4), and the instrument now exists — import_sieve, built 2026-08-06 — so the guard is a `forbidden` rule declared at this device's own address (it imports nothing from the shared inspection library), which is NOT YET DECLARED and is the only thing this edge still owes. Kin sites that argue the same distinction and never named it: logger-for-bash ('booting is precisely the moment when nothing else is up yet to observe you') and transitions.py summoning build_inspector LAZILY to stay out of boot order.

(f) THE INSPECTOR IS A BREAKPOINT, NOT A SERVICE — recorded 2026-08-06 because CC got this wrong on disk and the wrong reading is the kind that quietly becomes a build order. CC measured that nothing calls the inspector, nothing wires a receiver, and no emit() site carries a SEED key, and reported it as 'the supply side is zero' with a recommended sequencing (fat tier + wired receiver before more demand-side work). Akien: 'huh? of course, nothing calls the diagnostic inspector. it's like a breakpoint that you add when you need it.' ZERO STANDING CALLERS IS THE RESTING STATE. The instrument is ARMED BY HAND at debug time — wire a receiver, place or fatten the emit() at the gate under suspicion, fire, read, TAKE IT DOWN (the discipline DiagnosticBase.emit already states: 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging: a permanent firehose turns CC's mailbox into noise'). So there is nothing to sequence and no wiring owed: a debugger you have not attached is not a broken debugger. WHAT THE THREE MEASUREMENTS ACTUALLY MEAN, re-read correctly: no standing caller = correct; no wired receiver = correct, that is the attach step; thin standing emits carrying no SEED keys = also correct, because the SEED describes what a report ABOUT A FAULT must carry, and those values are supplied when the instrument is placed, not held permanently at every gate in the corpus. THE ONE THING THAT SURVIVES, and it is smaller and already filed as edge (a): the fat 30-day log tier serves the case a breakpoint cannot — a fault that ALREADY HAPPENED and will not reproduce, where there was no chance to place an instrument beforehand. That is a real second use case, not a prerequisite for the first, and it stays exactly where it was rather than being promoted by a misreading.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_inspector.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND the VALIDATION is persisted beside-code (validations/test_inspector.json) AND committed (git).
